newsitem.title: USA: Ford sees higher Q4 auto results, charges.
newsitem.headline: Ford sees higher Q4 auto results, charges.

text.p: Ford Motor Co Chairman Alex Trotman said Wednesday the company expects its automotive results to improve in the fourth quarter from the year before, despite $300 million to $400 million in additional charges that will be recorded to cover early retirement programs.
"We expect sales volumes will be higher and margins will improve," Trotman said in a statement accompanying the company's third quarter earnings release.
The U.S. No.2 automaker posted a third quarter net profit of $686 million, or $0.56 a fully diluted share, almost double the $357 million or $0.27 a share of the year before.
Commenting on the third quarter results, Trotman said improvements continue at Ford's U.S. auto operations, while Europe and South America still pose challenges for the company.

"There's still much to do. We've made solid progress, and we're becoming a leaner, faster company. As we continue to reduce costs and as more high-quality products are launched, automotive profitability should grow, increasing value for both customers and shareholders," he said in a statement.

Ford earned $634 million from its U.S. auto operations, but lost $619 million from non-U.S. auto units, for a total worldwide automotive profit of $15 million. A year ago, Ford lost $201 million from its worldwide auto units.
Trotman said Ford expects U.S. total vehicle sales to be 15.5 million for 1996, about in line with its earlier forecasts. The industry had 15.1 million in sales in 1995.

In Western Europe, Ford forecasts industry sales at 14.2 million for 1996, up from 13.4 million in 1995. Ford expects moderate economic growth to continue in its major worldwide markets, providing for stable industry sales volumes.
